A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViGaL study and contain readable main text, results, equations, and Appendices A–C. Content can be reliably matched despite substantial reorganization and localized layout defects.

before.justification: v1 reports original ViGaL gameplay evaluations, downstream benchmark results, ablations, math-data integration experiments, and pass@k analysis.

after.justification: v4 retains original ViGaL experiments and adds VSI-Bench results, inference-length measurements, and reasoning-trace analysis.

M1.justification: Both versions use Qwen2.5-VL-7B, RLOO without KL regularization, accuracy-plus-format rewards, and the same Snake and Rotation tasks and prompt templates. The format-reward section added to v4's appendix restates the existing rule. Two-stage game-then-math training already appears in v1 Appendix B.3.

E1.justification: v4 adds video-based 3D spatial reasoning on VSI-Bench, covering object counting, distances, object and room sizes, relative directions, route planning, and appearance order. This substantially extends evaluation requirements beyond the retained benchmarks. Snake, Rotation, MMK12, and the earlier downstream datasets remain.

E2.justification: The new VSI-Bench comparison includes previously unevaluated comparators such as Video-R1, Visual Jigsaw, LongVILA, LongVA, and Gemini-1.5 models. Conversely, InternVL2.5-8B and Llava-OV-7B are removed from the corresponding math, geometry, CLEVR+, and multi-discipline comparisons in Tables 2–3.

E3.justification: v4 introduces VSI-Bench evaluation using LMMs-Eval, greedy decoding, and 32 uniformly sampled video frames, plus a GPT-5 procedure extracting eight reasoning steps and rating nine mathematical aspects. The MathVerse analysis changes from nine-category Snake-versus-Rotation differences to eight-category comparisons against the base model. Existing training and benchmark protocols otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds inference-length analysis, paired game/math reasoning examples, and GPT-5 ratings of reasoning operations (Figure 4 and Appendices B.6–B.7). It removes v1 Figure 4's four training response-length ablation curves and revises the MathVerse subfield analysis. The main ablation tables, math-data integration, joint-game analysis, and pass@k study are retained.

E5.justification: v4 Table 2 first reports standard deviations from three independent runs for ViGaL Snake + Rotation. This is limited to that model's mathematical benchmark results and does not establish an increase over a stated v1 run count. The four independent Atari rollouts were already documented in v1.

E6.justification: Most retained benchmark scores are unchanged. v4 adds VSI-Bench scores (ViGaL 38.7, base model 36.7, Visual Jigsaw 38.5), inference lengths of 268 versus 250 tokens, and GPT-5 ratings. Subfield results are replaced: v1 Figure 5 favors Rotation on Length by 5.28 points, whereas v4 Figure 3 reports gains over the base model of 6.16 for Snake and 4.62 for Rotation. Figure 1's gains change from 1.5/1.0 to 2.9/2.4 points, and GPT-4o's Math average changes from 48.1 to 47.3.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation and mathematical content are retained. v4 Appendix A.3's piecewise format-reward equation is equivalent to v1's stated rule. The new GPT-5 rating rubric is an empirical analysis procedure, not a new theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: v4 explicitly extends the abstract's transfer claim to VSI-Bench 3D spatial reasoning. Its introduction also softens superiority over proprietary systems to competitive performance. The central claims about game-only RL, transfer to reasoning benchmarks, and preservation of general visual capabilities remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds the interpretation that improvements reflect transferable skills rather than verbosity and interprets GPT-5 ratings as evidence of mathematical operations in gameplay. It removes several arguments linking longer training responses to better reasoning or stability. The earlier limitation that the base model eventually achieves broader pass@k coverage remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 retains the main RL settings, hardware, resource links, and prompt templates, and adds VSI-Bench implementation details and the GPT-5 analysis prompt. However, Appendices A.1–A.2 omit v1's PPO optimizer/buffer details, 256-unit layer, precise initial rotations, example/task mesh allocation, and random selection of reasoning hints. These omissions do not establish changes to the underlying procedures.

R1.justification: v4 explicitly identifies Game-RL, cited through Code2logic, as the closest related work and adds references supporting video/spatial evaluation and inference-length discussion. It removes references including The Illusion of Thinking and CLEVR. The broader positioning of synthetic games against domain-specific post-training remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, game descriptions are merged and shortened, and method explanations and benchmark descriptions move into the appendices. Mathematical-data integration moves into the main results, while subfield analysis is reorganized. These changes substantially reshape the narrative beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the direct subfield chart with two baseline-relative charts, adds a reasoning-trace figure and new result tables, removes the training-length plots, and rearranges table groupings and ablation panels. Existing displays are also relocated. The retained case-study figure becomes crowded on page 30, overlapping the footer and clipping caption content.

improvement.justification: The added VSI-Bench evaluation with an explicit video protocol and Table 2's repeated-run uncertainty strengthen the empirical support for the retained generalization claim. Corrections to headline improvement arithmetic also improve reporting. The net gain is limited: reproduction details are omitted, token-length comparisons and GPT-5 ratings do not isolate transfer mechanisms, and the revised Length results conflict with the introduction's stronger Rotation-specific advantage.
